boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, documented destinations on Ithaca’s practical downtown and waterfront corridors.

cards.title: Ithaca Commons
cards.subtitle: East State Street / The Commons corridor
cards.notes: Walk the four-block pedestrian zone and use its seating areas as a starting point for downtown shops, performances, and public events.
cards.short_summary: A car-free downtown corridor with seating and performance space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Ithaca identifies the Commons as a four-block pedestrian-only zone with seating, shops, dining, a performance space, and events.
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian zone; individual businesses and programmed events may have separate access rules.

cards.title: Sagan Planet Walk
cards.subtitle: East State Street to 1st Street corridor
cards.notes: Start at the Sun station on the Commons and follow the marked scale-model route toward Pluto at the Sciencenter.
cards.short_summary: A 1.2-km outdoor scale model of the Solar System.
cards.evidence_claim: Sciencenter documents a 1.2-km scale-model walk beginning at the Commons’ Sun station and ending at Pluto at Sciencenter.
cards.access_notes: Follow the public outdoor route; a downloadable passport is available from Sciencenter.

cards.title: Tompkins Center for History & Culture
cards.subtitle: North Tioga Street / Bank Alley corridor
cards.notes: Use the center as a downtown orientation stop for exhibitions, visitor information, local art, and history-focused programming.
cards.short_summary: A downtown hub for art, tourism, education, and local history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tompkins Center for History & Culture describes itself as a downtown hub for exploration, art, tourism, and education at 110 North Tioga Street.
cards.access_notes: Located in Bank Alley on the Ithaca Commons; check the center’s site for current exhibition and event details.

cards.title: Tompkins County Public Library
cards.subtitle: East Green Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop in at 101 East Green Street for library services, then use the nearby Green Street transit stop for the next leg.
cards.short_summary: Downtown library access beside the Green Street transit corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Tompkins County Public Library is located at 101 East Green Street, and its page identifies the main Green Street bus stop as nearby.
cards.source_title: Location & Hours | Tompkins County Public Library
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8 p.m., Friday 9 a.m.–6 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; holiday closures apply.

cards.title: Cinemapolis
cards.subtitle: East Green Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the current schedule before heading to this downtown nonprofit cinema, whose programming includes independent, foreign, local, and documentary films.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit downtown cinema focused on independent and international film.
cards.evidence_claim: Cinemapolis describes itself as a nonprofit first-run independent theater in downtown Ithaca that programs independent, foreign, local, and documentary films.
cards.access_notes: Film schedule and ticket requirements vary; confirm showtime and rating before going.

cards.title: State Theatre of Ithaca
cards.subtitle: West State Street / MLK Jr. Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the calendar for an all-ages performance, then use the theatre’s official box office or ticket link for that specific show.
cards.short_summary: A historic downtown venue presenting concerts, films, comedy, dance, and community performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The State Theatre says it operates downtown Ithaca’s last remaining historic theater and hosts concerts, theater, comedy, films, dance, readings, and community performances.
cards.source_title: About Your State Theatre of Ithaca
cards.access_notes: Located at 107 West State Street; verify each event’s age policy, time, and ticket requirement before attending.

cards.title: DeWitt Park
cards.subtitle: North Cayuga Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause at the 1.66-acre downtown park, then notice how it anchors the surrounding historic district at North Cayuga and East Buffalo streets.
cards.short_summary: A compact downtown park at the center of a historic district.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s downtown plan places the 1.66-acre DeWitt Park at North Cayuga and East Buffalo Streets and notes it is maintained by the City.
cards.access_notes: Owned by First Presbyterian Church and maintained by the City of Ithaca, according to the City plan.

cards.title: Ithaca Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Third Street / Steamboat Landing corridor
cards.notes: Check the market calendar, then visit the Steamboat Landing pavilion at 545 Third Street to browse the scheduled vendor market.
cards.short_summary: A lakefront market pavilion at Steamboat Landing.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca Farmers Market lists its pavilion address as Steamboat Landing, 545 Third Street, Ithaca.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Ithaca Farmers Market
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current market day and vendor schedule before traveling to the pavilion.

cards.title: Sciencenter
cards.subtitle: 1st Street / Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Sagan Planet Walk endpoint as your cue to visit the museum’s interactive exhibits, outdoor Science Park, and science mini-golf.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on science museum at the end of the Sagan Planet Walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Sciencenter is located at 601 1st Street and reports more than 250 interactive exhibits plus a Science Park and science-themed mini-golf.
cards.access_notes: Published daily hours are 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; general admission is listed as $15, with specified free-admission exceptions.

cards.title: Cayuga Waterfront Trail
cards.subtitle: Cayuga Lake waterfront corridor
cards.notes: Use this waterfront route to link downtown with waterfront destinations, or connect northward toward the Black Diamond Trail from its trail network.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront trail connection serving Ithaca’s lakefront destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies the Cayuga Waterfront Trail as a connection to the Black Diamond Trail and describes it as part of the route between downtown and Cayuga Lake.
cards.access_notes: Use established trail sections and follow posted conditions and rules.
